topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool

scenario.topic: Decide which programming language for a new internal tool
scenario.opening_question: What trade-offs are we willing to make between development speed, maintainability, and integration?

options.name: Python 3.10 with FastAPI Framework
options.upside: Rapid prototyping and easy integration with APIs
options.tradeoff: Moderate runtime performance may limit scalability
options.concern: Some team members have limited experience with asynchronous Python

options.name: TypeScript with Node.js and Express
options.upside: Strong typing reduces bugs and good performance on backend
options.tradeoff: Longer initial setup and configuration time
options.concern: Requires more boilerplate and build tooling

options.name: Go 1.20 with Standard Library
options.upside: High performance and efficient concurrency handling
options.tradeoff: Steeper learning curve for team unfamiliar with Go
options.concern: Limited third-party libraries compared to other languages

options.name: C# with .NET Core 6
options.upside: Robust ecosystem and good tooling support
options.tradeoff: Requires Windows-based development environment for some tools
options.concern: Potential overhead in deployment and licensing concerns

shared_context: The tool must be ready within 3 months
The team size is exactly 4 developers
The tool will integrate with existing internal APIs and databases

personas.background: As a backend developer with moderate Python experience, Leo values rapid prototyping and API integration.
personas.private_goal: To choose a language that enables fast development and flexibility for evolving requirements.
